Rosh Hashanah Honey Cake (Lekach)

Served at: Rosh Hashanah (Jewish New Year)

Serves 12-16Prep 25 minCook 50-60 min

Honey cake, known as Lekach in Yiddish, is a quintessential dessert for Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year. Its rich, sweet flavor symbolizes the hope and prayer for a sweet and prosperous year ahead, making it a beloved centerpiece on holiday tables.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (240 ml) strong brewed coffee or black tea, cooled
  • 1 cup (240 ml) honey
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) vegetable oil
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) packed light brown sugar
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 2 1/2 cups (300 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • Optional: Sliced almonds for topping

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking pan or a 10-inch (25 cm) round bundt pan.
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together the cooled coffee (or tea), honey, vegetable oil, granulated sugar, brown sugar, eggs, and vanilla extract until well combined.
  3. In a separate medium bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, nutmeg, and salt.
  4. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined. Be careful not to overmix; a few lumps are fine.
  5. Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan. If desired, sprinkle the top with sliced almonds.
  6. Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. If using a bundt pan, baking time might be slightly longer.
  7. Let the cake cool in the pan on a wire rack for at least 15-20 minutes before inverting it onto the rack to cool completely.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, let the cake sit for 1-2 days before serving; the flavors deepen beautifully.
  • You can substitute orange juice for coffee/tea for a brighter, citrusy note.
  • Store the honey cake tightly wrapped at room temperature for up to 5 days, or freeze for longer storage.
